learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and abilities for the calculation, design, and testing of machines.
Applied knowledge of machine balancing and regulation systems.

Ability to draft and develop projects in the field of mechanical engineering, for the construction, reform, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacturing, installation, assembly or operation of: structures, mechanical equipment, energy installations, electrical installations, industrial installations and plants, and manufacturing processes.
Ability to manage activities that are the subject of the engineering projects described in the previous section.
Ability to perform measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert opinions, studies, reports, work plans and other similar tasks.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Ability to interpret technical projects and reports.
Ability to evaluate the effectiveness, viability, and quality of implemented solutions.
Demonstrate the ability to analyze and synthesize.
Acquire the ability to effectively solve problems.
Possess the ability to make decisions.
Develop critical reasoning.
Develop the ability to work in a team.
Ability to apply knowledge to practice.
Acquire the ability for autonomous learning and concern for knowledge and continuous training.
Ability to generate new ideas (creativity).
Ability to work autonomously.
Achievement motivation.
Enable the student to know the theory of mechanical vibrations.
Enable the student to control and isolate harmful machine vibrations.
Enable the student to perform static and dynamic balancing of rotary machines once manufactured.
Acquire knowledge of the kinematics and dynamics of rotary and reciprocating engines and their imbalances, as well as balancing processes.
Acquire knowledge of vibration measurement.
Enable the student to perform modal analysis using the finite element method.

syllabus_topics: Theory of free and forced mechanical vibrations
Free damped and undamped vibration of a translational and a torsional system
Harmonically excited vibration and forced vibration
Free and forced vibrations of 2 degrees of freedom
Determination of the PD2 of a machine
teaching_methods: Completion of personal and teamwork assignments
assessment_rules: The evaluation system for exchange students may be modified if the academic calendars of the home and host universities do not coincide. Conventional evaluation consists of a 40% final written theory exam, 40% final written problem exam, and 20% personal or teamwork supplement. Exceptional evaluation involves written final tests on official dates and the presentation and oral exposition of a personal work agreed with the professor. The percentages for final evaluation are the same for both conventional and exceptional evaluation.
